title: Level 1 (Beginner) - A-25
notes:
West leads the ♥Q which South wins. South has 8 top tricks (2 hearts and 6 diamonds). South does not have time to set up his ninth trick in spades. By the time a spade trick is established the defenders will be in a position to cash at least 3 heart tricks. 3 heart tricks along with the ♠A and ♠K will defeat the contract.

South must, therefore, look towards clubs for his ninth trick. If South leads a club up to North's ♣K at trick 2, a club trick can be taken any time West has the ♣A. This is another form of the simple finesse.

It would be a mistake to cash all of dummy's diamonds before leading clubs. The lead would end up in the wrong hand to take the club finesse. South's only remaining hand entry would be in hearts. Once South's second heart stopper is gone, West can simply take his ♣A and cash out hearts and spades.
